items.t: Softer bank, property earnings pull Ayala core profit down by 6%
Ayala profit weakens on softer cyclical businesses
sum: MANILA, Philippines — Softer results from its cyclical businesses weighed on Ayala Corp.’s core earnings in the first nine months, which slipped by six percent to P34.5 billion.

Ayala said stable earnings from Globe Telecom Inc., higher contributions from AC Energy and Infrastructure Corp. (ACEIC) and narrower losses from the emerging businesses helped temper the impact of softer results from its cyclical businesses, Ayala Land Inc. (ALI) and Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI), as well as lower non-operating income.

The decline in non-operating income mainly reflected reduced dividends from Manila Water as the first batch of divested Manila Water preferred shares had been fully transferred, and a smaller stake in Mynt after Mitsubishi Corp. invested in AM 50 Ventures Inc. in 2025.
On a reported basis, Ayala’s net income fell by 22 percent to P36.3 billion, reflecting a high 2025 base that included a one-off remeasurement gain on AM 50 Ventures.
“Our results reflect the benefits of strengthening and rebalancing the portfolio over the past several years,” Ayala CEO Cezar Consing said.
“Improving contributions from our growth platforms, narrowing losses from emerging businesses and disciplined capital allocation are helping build a more resilient earnings base,” he said.
BPI saw its net income inch down by three percent to P48.9 billion as higher provisions and operating expenses offset double-digit loan growth and higher fee income.

PSP Investments buying 50% Enercare stake, pension investor group buying interest in Mitsubishi’s Canadian LNG business
sum: The Public Sector Pension Investment Board is acquiring a 50 per cent interest in Enercare Inc. from Brookfield and its institutional partners for $1.6 billion.

Enercare is a Canadian home infrastructure platform providing critical equipment, including water heaters, heating, ventilation and air conditioning equipment, water purification systems and protection plans for more than one million homes in Canada.

In a press release, both partners said they are committed to support Enercare’s plans to expand its customer base and introduce new products and services. In the release, Andrew Alley, managing director and global head of infrastructure investments at PSP Investments, said the asset is a highly attractive long-term infrastructure investment.

“Held within our high inflation correlated infrastructure portfolio, it will rank among our most significant direct infrastructure investments in Canada, reflecting our conviction in investing where our local knowledge, relationships, and experience provide a distinct advantage.”

A group of Canadian pension fund investors — CPP Investments, the Investment Management Corp. of Ontario, the Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System and PSP Investments — is gaining access to Mitsubishi Corp.’s liquefied natural gas business in Canada.

Through a partnership with Blackstone Inc., the group will acquire a 49.9 per cent non-controlling interest in a Mitsubishi subsidiary, which holds interest in a liquefied natural gas Canada liquefaction business. The transaction will result in the group investing $3.1 billion for its stake with Mitsubishi retaining its controlling partner status and its full share of LNG offtake, according to a press release.

“LNG Canada is a high-quality, globally strategic asset with strong long-term fundamentals and attractive return potential for the CPP Fund,” said Geoff Souter, managing director and head of real assets credit at CPP Investments, in the release. “We see this as a compelling opportunity to invest at scale here in Canada alongside Mitsubishi, Blackstone and our Canadian peers.”

Berkshire to Reissue Yen-Denominated Bonds, Taps Mizuho and BofA as Lead Underwriters
sum: U.S. investment firm Berkshire Hathaway is preparing to issue yen-denominated bonds, it emerged on the 9th. It has tapped Mizuho Securities and BofA Securities as lead underwriters and is considering a bond sale in the near future. Details such as the issue amount and maturities have not been decided at this point.

Since first issuing yen-denominated bonds in 2019, Berkshire has continued to sell bonds every year. Most recently, in April it raised a total of ¥272.3 billion (approximately $1.7 billion) through six tranches with maturities ranging from 3 to 30 years. This would be an additional issuance following that deal.

The company has used the funds raised through yen bonds to invest in Japanese companies, including shares in the five major trading houses such as Mitsubishi Corporation and Mitsui and Co., as well as Tokio Marine Holdings shares.

Some market participants are watching whether the company can issue at a scale comparable to previous deals, noting that investors' risk tolerance has declined against the backdrop of large interest-rate fluctuations.
Note: The most recent issuance track record is the April deal. The timing and scale of the current issuance have not been disclosed.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Begins Rebound as U.S. Stock Gains and Oil Price Plunge Offer Support, but AI and Semiconductor Shares Weigh
sum: The Nikkei 225 began trading higher on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on November 5, opening at 62,384.73 yen, up 196.10 yen (0.32%) from the previous trading day. Buying led the market, carrying over the momentum from gains in all three major U.S. stock indexes the prior day.

Two factors pushed the market up. One was the firm performance of the U.S. stock market as it digested the results of the U.S. midterm elections. The other was a sharp drop in crude oil prices as views spread that tensions in the Middle East were easing. Lower energy costs support investor sentiment through both corporate earnings and household burdens.
Among blue-chip shares, Toyota Motor (7203.T) surged, while Sony Group (6758.T) and index-heavyweight Fast Retailing (9983.T) were quoted higher.

On the other hand, artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor-related shares saw notable declines. SoftBank Group (9984.T), Tokyo Electron (8035.T), and Advantest (6857.T) all fell sharply, as caution over the direction of AI regulation continued to simmer.

In the previous day's trading on November 4, these three semiconductor and AI-related stocks alone pushed the Nikkei 225 down by about 1,241 yen at one point. Selling tends to concentrate in stocks with large index weightings, and this structure continues to amplify swings across the broader market.

Among market participants, the near-term focus is whether buybacks will emerge in the sharply fallen semiconductor shares. On the previous day, some stocks such as Fast Retailing and Nintendo (7974.T) rose, so the market was not uniformly lower. Some see the fact that buying interest is not one-sided as a sign of the market's underlying resilience.

On the overseas front, reports on vote counting in the U.S. midterm elections were also coming in during Tokyo trading hours, and market participants are focused on how U.S. long-term interest rates and foreign exchange rates react. Domestically, earnings announcements from companies such as IHI (7013.T), Mitsubishi Corp (8058.T), and NTT (9432.T) are scheduled during trading hours, and stock price reactions to individual earnings results could divide winners and losers within sectors.

Mitsubishi Corp Lifts Full-Year Profit Target to Record ¥1.2 Trillion, Unveils ¥1 Trillion Buyback
sum: Mitsubishi Corp (8058.T) now expects consolidated net income of ¥1.2 trillion (about $7.6 billion) for the fiscal year ending March 2027, a ¥100 billion increase over its previous guidance and a record for the Japanese trading house. The new target, announced Wednesday, tops the ¥1.175 trillion average of 12 analyst estimates compiled by IBES.

The company also authorized share repurchases of up to ¥1 trillion (about $6.3 billion), lifting the maximum it plans to spend on buybacks this fiscal year. It kept its annual dividend forecast at ¥125 per share.

First-half results gave the company room to raise its outlook. Net income for the six months through September jumped 74% to ¥619.7 billion (about $3.9 billion) from ¥355.8 billion a year earlier. Underlying operating cash flow advanced 63% to ¥728.1 billion (about $4.6 billion), helped by market conditions and progress in recycling capital.

Mineral resources earnings were lifted by higher copper prices and stronger Australian steelmaking coal prices. The energy and power segment gained from increased liquefied natural gas transactions and dividend income, and the company booked gains from asset sales and other one-time items.
The upgraded cash flow forecast now stands at ¥1.38 trillion (about $8.7 billion), up from ¥1.25 trillion, with both profit and cash flow projected to set records.
Not every business is improving. Mitsubishi flagged cost pressure and softer conditions in some operations, including salmon farming and overseas grain trading.
Note: First-half net income was ¥619.7 billion (about $3.9 billion), up 74% year on year; first-half underlying operating cash flow was ¥728.1 billion (about $4.6 billion), up 63%.

New investors spend $3.1 billion US buying into LNG Canada's expansion plans
sum: Canadian pension funds will be among the new investors in LNG Canada’s Kitimat export terminal after one of the venture’s joint partners sells off part of its stake in the development.

Mitsubishi Corp., which owns 15 per cent of LNG Canada, said Monday that it is selling 49.9 per cent of its subsidiary that owns the stake in the liquefied natural gas export plant to an investor group led by U.S. private-equity firm Blackstone, which said the group will be spending $3.1 billion US for the share.

Blackstone said funds managed by its Blackstone Credit & Insurance division will be buying into the development, along with the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System, Investment Management Corp. of Ontario, and Public Sector Investment Board.
CPP Investment Board executive Geoff Souter called LNG Canada “a high-quality, globally strategic asset” with the potential to deliver attractive returns to its funds.
“We see this as a compelling opportunity to invest at scale in Canada alongside Mitsubishi, Blackstone and our Canadian peers,” said Souter, CPP Investment’s managing director.

In a statement, Mitsubishi said the sale of the stake, which it estimated is worth $1.6 billion US, doesn’t change its agreement with the project, which calls for Mitsubishi to receive 2.1 million tonnes per year of LNG Canada’s 14-million-tonnes-per-year capacity. Mitsubishi will invite new investment from Blackstone and its partners for LNG Canada’s major expansion.
LNG Canada, a $40 billion investment led by Shell, became Canada’s first LNG export plant in 2025 when it shipped its first cargo from Kitimat, 640 kilometres northwest of Vancouver.

items.t: Blackstone, Canadian pension funds invest $3.1-billion for LNG Canada stake
sum: Blackstone Inc. BX-N and four major Canadian pension funds are paying US$1.6-billion to buy a minority stake in a Mitsubishi Corp. subsidiary that owns a share of LNG Canada’s liquefaction business, and investing a further US$1.5-billion to help fund expansion plans as part of the deal.

Mitsubishi owns a 15-per-cent stake in LNG Canada through a subsidiary and will stay the controlling partner of that entity. The investor group is acquiring a 49.9-per-cent interest in the Mitsubishi subsidiary, and committing to $3.1-billion in total investment.

Blackstone is leading the investor group that includes Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System, Investment Management Corp. of Ontario and the Public Sector Pension Investment Board.

LNG Canada operates the country’s first natural-gas export terminal, an $18-billion facility in Kitimat, B.C., that opened in June, 2025. Under the deal announced Monday, Mitsubishi will continue its agreement to offtake 2.1 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas annually from LNG Canada.
Earlier this year, both Mitsubishi and LNG Canada’s largest shareholder, Shell PLC, considered reducing their stakes to raise funds for expansion plans.

Mitsubishi hired Royal Bank of Canada’s capital markets arm to pursue a deal and both shareholders were reportedly fielding bids as early as this summer from U.S.-based asset managers such as Blackstone and Apollo Global Management Inc.
However, Shell is no longer pursuing a similar transaction, at least in the near term, three sources with knowledge of the process said.

Japan Stocks Face Volatile Start to November
sum: TOKYO - Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 index enters trading on November 2 after closing at 63,290.11 on October 30, down 1,369.36 points, or 2.12%, in its final session of October, as selling in artificial intelligence and semiconductor-related stocks raised concerns about the sustainability of the technology-led rally, while investors prepared for a shortened trading week dominated by corporate earnings, monetary policy developments and the US midterm elections.

The sharp decline on October 30 followed three consecutive sessions of gains and reflected renewed uncertainty over the enormous capital expenditure required to support the global expansion of artificial intelligence. Japanese semiconductor stocks were particularly vulnerable to weakness in US technology shares, while some domestic-oriented companies showed greater resilience.

The Nikkei ended October down 5.19% from its September 30 close of 66,753.72, while the broader TOPIX index declined 3.49% over the month to 3,965.07. The reversal followed a strong start to October, when the Nikkei climbed above 70,000 before investors began reassessing valuations and the earnings outlook for AI-related businesses.

Despite the turbulence, Japanese stocks have shown substantial differences in performance between sectors. Semiconductor manufacturers, testing equipment companies and suppliers to the global technology industry have experienced pronounced swings, reflecting uncertainty over the pace and profitability of AI investment. Domestic businesses, including some consumer and pharmaceutical companies, have attracted buyers seeking alternatives to highly valued technology shares.

The Bank of Japan remains another important influence on financial markets after leaving its benchmark policy rate unchanged at approximately 1.25% at its October 30 policy meeting. Investors are assessing whether persistent inflation, wage developments and changes in the yen could encourage further tightening, particularly as higher borrowing costs affect corporate investment, household consumption and government debt financing.

items.t: Ayala approves charter overhaul to pave way for ₱44-billion Mitsubishi partnership
Mitsubishi's P44.5-B Ayala deal clears key shareholder hurdle
sum: At a special meeting on Oct. 27, Ayala shareholders cleared amendments that will expand the company's board from seven to nine directors and create a new class of voting shares to accommodate Mitsubishi's investment.

The company also elected Alberto M. de Larrazabal, former Ayala chief finance officer and current AREIT president and CEO, and Delfin L. Lazaro, former Philippine energy secretary and Ayala finance chief, to fill the two additional board seats.

Under the agreement announced in September, Mitsubishi will increase its economic ownership in Ayala from 4.7 percent to 15 percent, while its voting stake will climb to 20 percent, giving the Japanese group greater influence over the conglomerate's direction.

To make that possible, shareholders approved reclassifying 1.44 million unissued common shares into 71.86 million voting preferred shares, alongside changes to shareholder rights and provisions governing future share conversions.
The transaction will also bring about P20 billion directly into Ayala, which plans to use the money to reduce debt, purchase shares and finance future growth.
The broader P44.5-billion deal includes a voluntary tender offer for up to 30 million Ayala shares at P650 apiece, allowing existing shareholders to sell at a premium.
Ayala and Mitsubishi have worked together since 1974, with the expanded partnership targeting infrastructure, renewable energy, real estate, digital technology, mobility and logistics.

Mitsubishi Corp is Japan's largest general trading house, or sogo shosha, operating a diversified portfolio of businesses worldwide. Nikkei Stock Average rebounds sharply, closes up 806 yen at 65,020 on U.S. stock gains and short covering
sum: The Nikkei Stock Average (225 issues) rebounded sharply on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on September 4, closing at 65,020.94, up 806.46 points from the previous day, reclaiming the 65,000 level. Following broad gains across major U.S. equity indexes in the prior session, buying spread across the Tokyo market, led by tech stocks. With the index having fallen for four consecutive sessions through the previous day, short covering in stocks perceived as attractively valued also provided support.
The Tokyo Stock Price Index (TOPIX) finished at 4,103.23, up 1.19 points. Trading volume totaled approximately 2.21 billion shares.

The upward momentum was evident from the morning session. The morning close stood at 64,769.74, up 555.26 points from the previous day, with gains at one point exceeding 600 points. The TOPIX was down 7.56 points at 4,094.48, reflecting a mixed picture where large-cap stocks attracted buying while some small- and mid-cap issues saw profit-taking.

The key catalyst for the rally was a speech by Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller. Market expectations for near-term rate hikes receded, triggering a rebound in U.S. equities. That momentum spilled over into the Tokyo market, driving capital inflows into semiconductor-related and other tech stocks.

The previous day's session on September 3 had lacked clear direction. While buying emerged on relief that the rise in long-term interest rates had paused, concerns over a global economic slowdown amid persistent inflation served as a selling catalyst, leaving the morning close at 64,455, up just 130 points. Uncertainty over the Middle East situation also weighed on sentiment.

In the morning session on September 3, SoftBank Group (9984.T) was the top positive contributor to the Nikkei, adding 116.66 points to the index. Tokyo Electron (8035.T) followed with a contribution of 40.23 points, and Mitsubishi Corp (8058.T) added 23.63 points. On the negative side, Fast Retailing (9983.T) was the largest drag, subtracting 190.67 points, followed by Advantest (6857.T) at 57.93 points and Ibiden (4062.T) at 43.58 points.
By sector, 23 of the 33 industry groups on the Tokyo Stock Exchange advanced, with wholesale trade, oil and coal products, steel, and securities and commodity futures leading the gainers.

Japan’s Mitsubishi Becomes One of the Largest Gas Producers in the US
sum: Mitsubishi Corporation has completed its acquisition of US shale gas producer Aethon Energy, closing the $7.2 billion transaction first announced in January. The deal is the largest acquisition in the Japanese trading and investment firm's history.

In a statement issued 14 July, Aethon Energy said the transaction transfers to Mitsubishi all equity interests in two of its subsidiaries, along with a newly named upstream and midstream operating company, Adamas Energy, which is wholly owned by Mitsubishi.

Aethon said it will continue to operate as a private investment company and owner-operator of oil and natural gas fields along with sustainable energy projects. The Dallas-based company said it also plans to acquire a 25% nonoperating working interest in the assets it has sold to Mitsubishi. The repurchase of those assets is subject to regulatory approvals and the availability of financing.

“Aethon is pleased to continue our partnership with Mitsubishi through our global strategic alliance and we look forward to exploring new opportunities together. With our experienced team, significant investment capacity, and proven approach to value creation, we believe Aethon is well positioned to pursue a wide range of compelling opportunities across energy and infrastructure,” Gordon Huddleston, president and CEO of Adamas,” said in a statement.
Prior to the acquisition, Aethon was the largest privately held gas producer in the Haynesville Shale and North America.

Earlier this month, energy analytics firm Enverus ranked Aethon as the third-largest private producer in the US based on total energy output, behind Continental Resources and Mewbourne Oil. The company averaged 2.65 Bcf/D, or 443,000 BOE/D, of production in 2025.

The Mitsubishi acquisition follows other recent moves by Japanese companies into the US shale gas sector, which have been viewed as broad efforts to secure long-term liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies.

Sumitomo Corp Soars on 4-for-1 Stock Split and ¥80 Billion Buyback; Net Profit Set for Second Straight Record
sum: Sumitomo Corp (8053.T) announced large-scale shareholder return measures and a stock split on the 1st, triggering a sharp surge in its share price. Consolidated net profit under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for the fiscal year ending March 2027 is forecast at ¥630 billion, up 5% from the previous year, marking a second straight record high. The earnings outlook exceeded prior analyst estimates, and combined with the 4-for-1 stock split and a share buyback of up to ¥80 billion, the stock was bought up as much as 16% intraday.

The ¥630 billion net profit forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027—the final year of the newly announced medium-term management plan—came in slightly above market expectations. The average analyst forecast compiled by QUICK Consensus was ¥624.1 billion, and it also cleared the ¥624.9 billion average net profit estimate from 13 analysts polled by IBES. Full-year consolidated net profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 disclosed simultaneously came in at ¥600.3 billion, up 6.8% year-on-year, exceeding the company's own forecast of ¥570 billion by more than ¥30 billion. Even amid ongoing fluctuations in resource prices, the company's diversified business portfolio contributed to an uplift in earnings.

The centerpiece of the shareholder return policy is a 4-for-1 stock split effective July 1. By lowering the minimum investment amount, the company aims to enhance share liquidity and expand its investor base, particularly among individual investors. The annual dividend forecast is ¥40 on a post-split basis. Compared to the pre-split actual dividend of ¥150 for the previous fiscal year, this effectively represents a dividend increase.

Furthermore, Sumitomo will implement a share buyback of up to ¥80 billion. The repurchase period runs for approximately 11 months, from May 7 through March 31, 2027. The acquisition ratio relative to total shares outstanding was not disclosed, but the market expects improvements in capital efficiency and an uplift in earnings per share.

Following the announcement, buy orders flooded in for Sumitomo Corp shares on the Tokyo market. The stock price skyrocketed immediately after the release, at one point surging 16% from the previous day's close.

items.t: Anglo American draws three bidders for coal sale
sum: Anglo American (LON: AAL) is said to have at least three potential buyers for its Australian steelmaking coal business after a $3.8 billion sale to Peabody Energy (NYSE: BTU) collapsed following a mine fire.

Stanmore Resources (ASX: SMR), Mitsubishi Corp., and Indonesia’s BUMA Internasional are among at least three bidders circling the Queensland-based assets, with a deal potentially emerging in the coming months, according to Bloomberg News. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are running the process, the news outlet’s sources said.

The sale’s collapse last year dealt a setback to Anglo’s broader plan to divest non-core assets after BHP’s (ASX: BHP) failed takeover bid, and a successful deal now would help revive that strategy while potentially reshaping the global steelmaking coal market.

Peabody walked away from the agreement after a fire at the Moranbah North mine, which it said accounted for roughly half the deal’s value. The incident followed another blaze in 2024 at the Grosvenor mine, Anglo’s second-largest metallurgical coal operation, which remains offline even as Moranbah North has resumed production.

For bidders, acquiring the portfolio would either cement or elevate their standing among the world’s top suppliers of steelmaking coal to Asian markets, currently dominated by the BHP Mitsubishi Alliance and Glencore (LON: GLEN). Buma Internasional already has exposure to the assets, having agreed to acquire a 51% stake in the Dawson project from Peabody contingent on the original deal’s completion.

Stanmore, backed by Indonesia’s Widjaja family through Golden Energy and Resources, may face financing pressure if it proceeds, as its market capitalization sits below A$2 billion, potentially less than the transaction value.

Anglo has already spun off its platinum division into Valterra Platinum (JSE: VAL) and continues to seek a buyer for its struggling De Beers, which is part of a sweeping portfolio overhaul as it advances the takeover of Canada’s Teck Resources (TSX: TECK.A TECK.B)(NYSE: TECK).

Per the agreement, Mitsubishi will use JPMorgan's blockchain platform, Kinexys, to manage payments across its global operations. This growing adoption indicates that blockchain is now integrated into the core operations of large financial institutions.

The U.S. traditional financial industry is gradually shifting toward faster and more technology-driven systems. Blockchain is becoming an important tool in this transformation. It is helping institutions improve efficiency, reduce costs, and manage global transactions more effectively.

Kinexys is JPMorgan's blockchain-based platform, launched in 2020. It has already processed more than $3 trillion in transactions. The platform currently handles $5 billion in daily payments, and JPM aims to double this daily transaction value to $10 billion.

Zack Chestnut, the global head of business development for Kinexys, said, "Our goal is to meaningfully grow these figures as quickly as we can, we would be pleased but not satisfied to see daily transaction value get above $10 billion per day in the foreseeable future."

The platform offers several benefits. It enables near-instant fund transfers. It reduces reliance on intermediaries. It improves efficiency in cross-border payments. These features are especially useful for large companies operating across multiple regions.

JPMorgan also uses deposit-based digital tokens on this platform. These tokens are backed by funds held in bank accounts. They function similarly to stablecoins and allow faster and more secure transactions.

The expansion is expected to benefit JPMorgan in multiple ways. Higher transaction volumes can drive fee-based income growth. Increased adoption by global clients can strengthen the bank's payments business. It can also improve client retention by offering faster and more efficient services. Over time, continued investment in blockchain infrastructure may provide a strong competitive edge.

Nikkei to launch index with Buffett-inspired moat concept
sum: TOKYO -- Nikkei will begin calculating and publishing the Nikkei Moat Stock Index on Feb. 9. The innovative gauge will target Japanese companies with strong technological capabilities or brand power that can sustain high profitability over the medium to long term. These are seen as having an economic moat -- a concept that has drawn attention from prominent investors such as Warren Buffett. The new index selects such stocks using rules-based, quantitative criteria.

Among companies listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's Prime Market, the index first screens for stocks whose sales rank in the top 20% of their industry and whose market capitalization is at least 100 billion yen. It then selects 30 names whose operating cash flow margins -- a gauge of cash generation -- exceed the industry average by the largest margins. The premise is that companies turning a high sales share into cash are regarded as having an economic moat.

When adding new constituents, the index also looks at the PEG ratio, which incorporates earnings growth into the forward price-to-earnings ratio. The design aims to select companies that have economic moats while avoiding stocks that are overpriced.
Initial constituents will include Mitsubishi Corp., Tokyo Electron and Central Japan Railway.

items.t: Qantas Airways to exit Jetstar Japan, sharpen focus on domestic market
sum: as the flagship airline moves away from its budget international businesses to focus on core

The decision to sell its 33.32 per cent stake in Jetstar Japan comes after the closure of its Singapore-based Jetstar Asia in July as Qantas grappled with intense regional competition and high fuel and supplier costs, resulting in underwhelming performance.

The move will also enable Qantas to focus resources on its core operations in Australia, Qantas and Jetstar Airways, even as it undertakes its largest fleet renewal programme ever while grappling with slower-than-expected growth.

In November, it forecast domestic unit revenue growth at the lower end of its 3 per cent-5 per cent earlier projection for the six months to December 2025, with capacity constrained by delays in returning its A380s to service.

and Tokyo Century Corp will retain their 50 per cent and 16.7 per cent stakes, respectively, while the Development Bank of Japan intends to join as a shareholder, the companies said in a joint statement on Tuesday.
Jetstar Japan was established more than a decade ago by Qantas, Japan Airlines, and Mitsubishi Corp. It began operating as a low-cost carrier in late 2012 out of Narita airport near Tokyo.
The new shareholder group, entirely made up of Japanese investors, intends to overhaul and rebrand Jetstar Japan and expand its international routes, the companies said.
